description.narrative: By the end of the programme, the British Council is expected to have supported up to nine migration-affected communities in formulating recommendations concerning migration policies and practices. The key community engagement strategy will be to establish platforms for multi-stakeholder dialogue between migrants, host communities and government officials responsible for migration management at national and sub-national levels.

Ethiopia - Pre-identified CSOs from BMM phase 1, Government partners may include: local officials at the woreda and zonal level, and the National Partnership Coalition (NPC) whose members include Attorney General office, Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MOLSA), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA), Immigration, Nationality and Vital Events Agency (INVEA), Central statistics Agency (CSA), Federal job Creation Commission (JCC) and International organization for Migration (IOM), as well as Regional Anti-Trafficking Task Force(s) (RTFs) in implementation locations, other regional entities, such as the Women Children and Youth (BoWCY) as required. Pre-identified CSOs from phase 1: Sudanese Organisation for Research and Development (SORD), Sudanese Development Call Organisation (NIDAA), Sudan Environment Conservation Society (SECS) Government partners* MoI, MoFA, Ministry of Labour and Social Development, Ministry of Justice, NCCT, National Council of Population, Centre of migration studies, local governments. * any new committees/institutions the new government shall establish, migration and Civil record institution, Central Bureau of Statistics. "

The primary objective of the project is to enable migration affected communities to formulate recommendations on their needs and priorities with regards to migration management towards national resource allocation.

This project has a specific focus on working with and for communities, to improve their access to services that respond to their needs. At the heart of our approach is an emphasis on empowerment of citizens; building capacity of local stakeholders; fostering dialogue across and between communities, local authorities and civil society; and building trust and legitimacy. We will apply a cultural relations approach to promote dialogue, development, collaboration and co-operation on issues that are of local importance to communities – often across societal divides and in some of the most fragile contexts.
